references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, the waving (תְּנוּפָה) of the offering before the Lord's presence is described, which is the same ritual performed with the breast.
Describes how the breast of the wave offering belongs to Aaron and his sons and must be waved before the Lord's presence.
Confirms that the wave breast and the raised thigh are given to Aaron and his sons as their portion from the Israelites.
Moses took the breast and waved it as a wave offering before the Lord from the consecration ram, in parallel with the instruction here.
Affirms that the wave breast and the raised thigh must be eaten in a clean place and belong to the priest and his family.
The priest shall wave the offering as a wave offering before the Lord; it is holy and belongs to the priest along with the wave breast.
The meat of the wave offering belongs to the priest, just like the wave breast and the right thigh.
Explains how the instruction in Exodus was fulfilled by Aaron during the first sacrificial ritual.
Places the specific consecration ritual in Exodus within the general law for the thank offering.
Explains the eternal theological consequence of 'your portion' given in the consecration ritual.
